briefing:
The Suwalki Gap Crisis enters its final phase. The London co-guarantor trilateral has produced a workable enforcement mechanism for the Istanbul Accord, with the CEP initialed at Lancaster House. Milestone 1 certification is expected within 48 hours following EU Council initiation of formal review, with Hungarian acquiescence secured through structural fund commitments. Russia's Belarus withdrawal is ahead of schedule, with full completion within 6-8 days.

The permanent NATO force posture on the eastern flank is crystallizing: German brigade at Rukla (EUR 3.2B Zeitenwende East), Canadian permanent basing at Camp Adazi, UK STEADFAST GUARDIAN at Tapa and Bardufoss, and US V Corps permanence at Poznan-Krzesiny. The Weimar Triangle summit on Day 11 will address trilateral military coordination, integrated air defense for the Suwalki corridor, and EU defense industrial cooperation.

Economically, oil approaches $96 as Milestone 1 certification becomes imminent. Baltic shipping insurance surcharges fall to 15% as commercial traffic reaches 70% of pre-crisis levels. European gas prices return to pre-crisis baseline. The economic normalization track is accelerating.

Key questions for the final phase: Will Milestone 1 be formally certified? Can the US and Russia finalize the Geneva cyber restraint framework? Will the Weimar Triangle produce concrete commitments on permanent trilateral coordination? And can nuclear posture de-escalation be structured as a Milestone 2 condition acceptable to all parties?
narrative:
Day 10 of the Suwalki Gap Crisis marked the transition from crisis management to post-crisis order-building, with the London co-guarantor trilateral summit as the day's centerpiece. PM Starmer hosted President Macron and President Erdogan at Lancaster House for a full day of negotiations on the Co-Guarantor Enforcement Protocol (CEP). The talks were constructive but contentious: Turkey demanded a consensus requirement for enforcement actions (effective veto power), while the UK and France pushed for a qualified majority mechanism. After six hours of negotiation, a compromise emerged: enforcement actions below military force require two-of-three co-guarantor agreement; military enforcement requires unanimity plus UNSC authorization under Resolution 2741. Turkey accepted the compromise after receiving assurances on F-16 deliveries and a commitment to rotate the quarterly summit to Ankara. The CEP was initialed at Lancaster House at 22:00 CET.

Milestone 1 certification advanced decisively. SIPRI's formal recommendation, backed by BND intelligence assessments and Czech Verification Ladder data, was presented to the EU Council. Lithuania's formal request received support from all member states except Hungary, which demanded accelerated sanctions relief as a condition for acquiescence. After intense diplomatic pressure from Germany and France, Budapest agreed to support Milestone 1 certification in exchange for a commitment to begin EU structural fund reallocation discussions within 30 days. The EU Council initiated formal Milestone 1 review, with certification expected within 48 hours.

Russia continued to exceed Istanbul Accord compliance requirements. The third echelon of the Belarus withdrawal -- logistics units at the Grodno assembly area -- began final rail movement to Smolensk, putting full withdrawal on track for completion within 6-8 days, well ahead of the 14-day deadline. Kaliningrad garrison remained in de-escalated posture with supply levels recovering to 9/10 through expanded Baltiysk corridor and Polish rail Phase 2 transit. Moscow accepted the US cyber restraint framework for civilian infrastructure at Geneva, though military C2 was excluded from scope. Russia signaled through London trilateral channels that nuclear posture de-escalation to peacetime would be considered as a Milestone 2 condition, contingent on reciprocal US de-escalation.

NATO's permanent eastern flank architecture continued to take shape at remarkable speed. Germany's Leopard 2A7 advance party at Rukla began integration with Lithuanian forces, with the Bundestag authorizing a comprehensive Zeitenwende East package of EUR 3.2B. Canada launched Camp Adazi permanent basing implementation. The UK's STEADFAST GUARDIAN package entered Parliamentary debate with strong cross-party support. The Baltic Defence Ministers trilateral position paper, Nordic NORDEFCO conference planning, and the Bucharest Nine summit preparation all pointed toward a fundamentally restructured NATO posture that would persist long after the immediate crisis faded.
